source: Original items modeling the Morningness-Eveningness construct (Horne & Ostberg, 1976). No MEQ or rMEQ items were used. Category names follow the MEQ convention.

scale.prompt_suffix: Not at all, a little, somewhat, mostly, or completely?

clock_scale.prompt_suffix: Just give me a time, like 'six thirty' or 'eleven p.m.'
clock_scale.parse: parseClockAnswer in scoring.ts: '7', '7:30', 'half past seven', '11 pm', '23:00', 'midnight'. A bare 1-6 for bedtime means after midnight; a bare 7-12 for bedtime means evening.

scoring_notes: Morningness 0-100. Agreement items: reverse negative polarity (6 minus answer), mean, map (mean - 1) / 4 * 100. Clock items: free-day wake time maps 05:00 -> 100 to 10:00 -> 0, free-day bedtime maps 21:00 -> 100 to 02:00 -> 0. Final score = 0.7 x agreement + 0.3 x clock when both exist. Cuts at 20 / 36 / 60 / 76 are the MEQ cuts (30 / 41 / 58 / 69 on 16-86) rescaled. Windows: natural wake = the clock answer, else 10:00 minus score / 100 x 5 h; natural bed = the clock answer, else wake minus 8 h; peak = wake + 2 h + (1 - score / 100) x 5 h, lasting 3 h. Confidence = distance from the nearest cut (8 points = full) times coverage, halved when the clock answers and the agreement items disagree by more than 35 points. See scoring.ts.

items.text: If you were completely free to plan your day, no work, no alarm, no one to look after, what time would you naturally get up?
And on that same free day, what time would you go to sleep?
I feel sharpest in the first few hours after I wake up.
I do my best thinking late in the evening, after most people have wound down.
Getting up early is easy for me, even without an alarm.
When I have to be up early, I feel groggy for a long time.
By ten at night I'm usually done. My brain switches off.
I could happily stay up past midnight most nights and not feel it the next day.
If I had a demanding two-hour task, I'd choose to do it in the morning.
A seven a.m. workout sounds awful. I'd rather train in the evening.
I'm hungry for breakfast within the first hour of waking.
On weekends I sleep in a lot later than on workdays.
